issues.description: Command names break the established singular-form naming convention
issues.detail: The new methods are named `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload` (plural), but every adjacent command uses the singular form: `quickmark_save`, `quickmark_load`, `quickmark_add`, `bookmark_add`, `bookmark_load`. The command surface now speaks two dialects for one concept, with no derivable rule distinguishing them. Rename to `quickmark_reload` / `bookmark_reload` to preserve consistency in the public command vocabulary.

issues.description: reload() is not atomic on parse failure — leaves marks silently empty
issues.detail: `reload()` calls `self.marks.clear()` first, then re-reads and parses line-by-line. If `_init_lineparser()` or `_parse_line()` raises (InvalidUrlError, IO error, malformed user edit), the manager is left empty with marks lost, `changed` never emitted, and no rollback. The correct shape is build-then-swap: parse into a new local OrderedDict, then atomically assign to `self.marks` on success. This makes failure non-destructive and the postcondition clear.

issues.description: reload() changes observable contract of __init__ by emitting `changed` during construction
issues.detail: Before this refactor, the constructor parsed inline and did NOT emit `self.changed`. After the refactor, `__init__` calls `reload()`, which emits `changed` at the end of construction. This is a behavior change not mentioned in the commit message. Either suppress `changed` on the initial load (parameterize reload with an emit flag), or explicitly document that construction emits `changed`. The signal semantics — emit exactly once per reload after `self.marks` reflects new state — should be stated as an invariant.

issues.description: Tests don't exercise reload()'s failure modes or interesting invariants
issues.detail: `test_reload` covers only the happy path: valid file replaced with another valid file. It does not test: (a) reload after the file is deleted, (b) reload with a malformed line, (c) reload that shrinks the mark set (deletions on disk), (d) that `changed` fires exactly once, (e) that the pre-reload state was actually loaded before reload. Add tests for these cases — they would also drive the atomicity fix and pin the 'disk is truth' semantics.

Both new Gherkin scenarios use bare `Scenario:` headers with no title, while every other scenario in `urlmarks.feature` has a descriptive title (e.g., `Scenario: Saving a quickmark (:quickmark-add)`). Failures in unnamed scenarios are less legible. Add titles like `Scenario: Reloading bookmarks (:bookmark-reload)` and `Scenario: Reloading quickmarks (:quickmark-reload)`.

`_init_lineparser` was previously called exactly once at construction. It is now called once at construction (via `reload()`) and again on every subsequent `reload()`. Its name and underscore prefix signal one-shot setup, but it is now invoked repeatedly. Either document that it is idempotent and constructs a fresh lineparser each call, rename it (e.g., `_open_lineparser` / `_load_lineparser`), or split construction-time setup from per-reload re-reading so the parser is built once and reused.

issues.description: Two near-identical command methods could share a parameterized implementation
issues.detail: `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload` are structurally identical: fetch a manager from objreg, call `.reload()`, emit an info message. They differ only in the objreg key and the message string. The `UrlMarkManager` supertype already factors the shared behavior at the model layer; the command layer duplicates the call site. Acceptable as-is for two instances; flag for a future refactor if a third mark variety is added.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the underlying refactor — lifting load logic into a shared `reload()` method on `UrlMarkManager` and having `__init__` delegate to it — is the right shape and good taste. Two issues block merge: the new command names (`quickmarks_reload` / `bookmarks_reload`) break the established singular convention used by every adjacent command, and `reload()` is non-atomic — it clears marks before parsing, leaving the manager silently empty on any parse failure. Additionally, `reload()` now emits `changed` during construction, a behavior change with no stated rationale or contract. Tests cover only the happy path and miss the interesting failure modes (malformed file, deleted file, deletions on disk, single-emit invariant). Minor polish: unnamed Gherkin scenarios, undocumented re-entrancy of `_init_lineparser`, and a future opportunity to deduplicate the two near-identical command methods.
